fr.elements: Main Building; Front Driveway; Access Road; Open Green Space; Landscaped Area; Dense Vegetation; Open Green Space; Detached Structure; Pedestrian Walkways; Street Frontage
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access; Long Driveway
fr.recommendations: Ensuring the front driveway and access road remain clear of obstructions could support unimpeded entry and exit for emergency apparatus, particularly given the single point of access serving the property. Maintaining adequate turning and staging space along the driveway would assist larger vehicles in maneuvering during an incident. Clearly marking the address at the street frontage could improve responder navigation during initial approach. The dense vegetation near the access corridor and rear of the property may limit visibility and movement for personnel working around the detached structure, so keeping travel pathways to and around both structures as open as practical could enhance operational effectiveness.

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Dense Shrub Cover; Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Fuel Continuity; Brush Adjacent to Structure; Ladder Fuels; Mixed Vegetation Cover; Brushland Interface; Single Access Route; Vegetation Adjacent to Access Route; Limited Defensible Space
wildfire.recommendations: Reducing the density of shrub cover immediately surrounding the structure and creating separation between ground-level brush and any overhanging tree canopy could meaningfully reduce fuel continuity and ladder fuel pathways near the building. Thinning vegetation within the immediate structure perimeter and clearing brush directly adjacent to exterior walls and under eaves would support defensible space and may reduce structure exposure. Where tree clusters exist near the structure, removing low-hanging limbs and reducing understory shrub density beneath the canopy could interrupt vertical fuel continuity. Managing vegetation along the single access route, including trimming encroaching brush and maintaining adequate width and vertical clearance, would support firefighter access and improve evacuation conditions. Given that a single access route serves the property, keeping that corridor clear of vegetation encroachment should be considered a priority. Continuing long-term vegetation management across the property perimeter could improve overall wildfire resilience and suppression support opportunities.
